title: Friends and Subsequences
statementMd:
Mike and !Mike are old childhood rivals, they are opposite in everything they do, except programming. Today they have a problem they cannot solve on their own, but together (with you) — who knows?

Every one of them has an integer sequences $*a*$ and $*b*$ of length $*n*$. Being given a query of the form of pair of integers $(*l*, *r*)$, Mike can instantly tell the value of ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0920a88f2ac4dba81380b09878666ff7866f884b.png) while !Mike can instantly tell the value of ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d56dda45a4398472592dffa7a16fe1581d45486a.png).

Now suppose a robot (you!) asks them all possible different queries of pairs of integers $(*l*, *r*)$ $(1 ≤ *l* ≤ *r* ≤ *n*)$ (so he will make exactly $*n*(*n* + 1) / 2$ queries) and counts how many times their answers coincide, thus for how many pairs ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2752e2e562831cd694ac00e4396fd36a3a890b8f.png) is satisfied.

How many occasions will the robot count?

## Input

The first line contains only integer $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$).

The second line contains $*n*$ integer numbers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($- 10^{9} ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — the sequence $*a*$.

The third line contains $*n*$ integer numbers $*b*_{1}, *b*_{2}, ..., *b*_{*n*}$ ($- 10^{9} ≤ *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — the sequence $*b*$.

## Output

Print the only integer number — the number of occasions the robot will count, thus for how many pairs ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2752e2e562831cd694ac00e4396fd36a3a890b8f.png) is satisfied.

## Note

The occasions in the first sample case are:

1.$*l* = 4$,$*r* = 4$ since $*max*{2} = *min*{2}$.

2.$*l* = 4$,$*r* = 5$ since $*max*{2, 1} = *min*{2, 3}$.

There are no occasions in the second sample case since Mike will answer $3$ to any query pair, but !Mike will always answer $1$.
statementZhMd:
Mike 和 !Mike 是从小一起长大的老对手，他们做任何事情都截然相反，唯独编程除外。今天，他们遇到了一个无法独自解决的问题，但如果和你一起——谁知道呢？

他们每个人都有一个长度为 $*n*$ 的整数序列 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$。给定一个形如一对整数 $(*l*, *r*)$ 的询问，Mike 可以立即告诉你 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0920a88f2ac4dba81380b09878666ff7866f884b.png) 的值，而 !Mike 可以立即告诉你 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d56dda45a4398472592dffa7a16fe1581d45486a.png) 的值。

现在，假设一个机器人（也就是你！）向他们询问所有不同的整数对 $(*l*, *r*)$ $(1 ≤ *l* ≤ *r* ≤ *n*)$（因此他总共会进行恰好 $*n*(*n* + 1) / 2$ 次询问），并统计他们的答案相同的次数，也就是满足 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2752e2e562831cd694ac00e4396fd36a3a890b8f.png) 的整数对数量。

机器人会统计多少次？

## 输入格式

第一行仅包含一个整数 $*n*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$）。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$- 10^{9} ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）——序列 $*a*$。

第三行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*b*_{1}, *b*_{2}, ..., *b*_{*n*}$（$- 10^{9} ≤ *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）——序列 $*b*$。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——机器人会统计的次数，也就是满足 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2752e2e562831cd694ac00e4396fd36a3a890b8f.png) 的整数对数量。

## 说明

第一个样例中的符合条件的情况为：

1.$*l* = 4$，$*r* = 4$，因为 $*max*{2} = *min*{2}$。

2.$*l* = 4$，$*r* = 5$，因为 $*max*{2, 1} = *min*{2, 3}$。

第二个样例中不存在符合条件的情况，因为 Mike 对任意询问都会回答 $3$，而 !Mike 总是回答 $1$。
